Here's the stuff that's not in my last gear post. My new Eskimo 33CC 8" 2 stroke ice auger(x-mas gift to myself), and my Sonar, and how I adapt it from summer to winter use.

The sonar is a Garmin striker 4, it's a cheap but amazing little unit and has always done me well, it's got quite a few features, and a flasher mode which is what I use ice fishing. In the summer the transducer is mounted to my trolling motor propeller, I just took it off and zip tied a piece of pool noodle around it to float and set the angle to it floats level. The battery box is just a standard plastic battery box, in the summer I run a big deep cycle to power my motor and the Sonar, in the winter I don't need that much wieght to carry around so I use a 12v battery from a powerwheels toy, wrapped in towels to keep it insulated and warm. Everything packs up neatly into the box and is easy to carry around from hole to hole.

Damn I can't believe I missed this post. How long have you been using that setup and how does it affect the fishing? I don't have one but I've seen people using them in youtube icefishing videos. It seems like it would feel very different to ice fish while staring at a little screen than to fish without one.

It's handy but has it's drawbacks, I love it mostly for checking depth when I drill holes, before I used to drop a line down then pull it up and count how many feet I pull up. It's handy though, it shows your lure while you jig it and shows any fish coming to check it out. Makes it like a bit of a video game. I just don't like being restricted to sitting beside it, I like drilling lots of holes and moving around, cutting firewood, I really only jig my lines once n a while. Fish are lethargic in the winter sometimes over jigging your line just chases them away. We're allowed 2 holes each up here so when me and my son go out we have 4 holes and it's only usefull on 1 at a time anyways, when I'm out alone I like it because then I can jig one line and deadstick a line fairly close by. In the summer mounted to my canoe is where the unit really shines, I wouldn't catch half the fish I do in the summer without it. but again I use it to map out the lake and not really to target fish, although fidning areas where fish like to hang out is a bonus. It's cheap to buy and worth every penny. I think I paid about 100$ for it on amazon.
